summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, atrial fibrillation, and recent MRSA catheter-related bacteremia was admitted for shortness of breath and generalized malaise after missing a dialysis session. She presented with hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and volume overload, but clear lungs on exam and imaging. She received two dialysis sessions, with improvement in symptoms and laboratory parameters. Her MRSA bacteremia was managed with continued vancomycin, and her anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation and IVC stenosis was maintained. Hypotension during dialysis was addressed with increased midodrine. She completed treatment for candidal esophagitis, and her HIV was stable on HAART. She was discharged home with services, on track to complete her antibiotic course, with follow-up planned for INR monitoring, eosinophilia evaluation, and primary care coordination.
